MCMC convergence and grid diagnostics for a fitted model

Source: R/diagnostics.R, R/methods.R, R/format-print.R
diagnose.Rd

diagnose() returns the MCMC diagnostics of a fit (R-hat, effective sample sizes, divergent transitions, tree depth and E-BFMI) and flags those that indicate a problem. The diagnostics were computed by bayes_efron_fit() when the model was fitted, so no sampling is done. diagnose() also checks the grid, in particular whether the result for any site depends on where the grid ends.

Usage

diagnose(fit, ...)

# Default S3 method
diagnose(fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
diagnose(fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_diagnostic'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_diagnostic'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_diagnostic'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_diagnostic'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
nuts_params(object, pars = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
log_posterior(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
rhat(object, pars = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_fit'
neff_ratio(object, pars = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

...

For diagnose(), these dots are for future extensions and must be empty. The print() method passes them on to format(); format() and summary() ignore them.

x, object

A bef_diagnostic object returned by diagnose(). For the bayesplot methods (nuts_params(), log_posterior(), rhat() and neff_ratio()), object is a bef_fit object.

row.names, optional

Ignored. They are arguments of the as.data.frame() generic.

use_cli

If TRUE and the cli package is installed, the first line is formatted in bold; FALSE gives plain text. If NULL (the default), the value of getOption("bayesEfron.use_cli", TRUE) is used.

pars

An optional character vector. For nuts_params(), the names of the sampler quantities to return; for rhat() and neff_ratio(), the names of the variables. If NULL (the default), all are returned.

Value

An object of class bef_diagnostic, which is a list with the following components.

rhat

R-hat for each variable in the draws, a named numeric vector.

ess_bulk, ess_tail

The bulk and tail effective sample sizes, in the same form.

divergences, max_treedepth

The number of divergent transitions and the number of iterations that reached the maximum tree depth, each summed over the chains.

ebfmi

The E-BFMI of each chain. Like the two counts, it is NA if CmdStan did not report it.

sampler_diagnostics_failed

Names of the diagnostics that fail a check.

sampler_diagnostics_warned

Names of the diagnostics that lead to a warning. "grid_ends" is among them if an end of the grid has the status "warning".

diagnostic_skipped

Names of the diagnostics that could not be computed or were not checked. These three character vectors are empty if the run has at least 400 draws and there are no problems.

grid

A list with the grid diagnostics (see below), or NULL if they cannot be computed for the fit.

model_family, stan_file_sha256, runtime_seconds, effective_params_summary

Values copied from fit$metadata (see bef_fit).

The list grid has the following components.

ends

A data frame with one row per end of the grid (see below).

share

The outer fraction of the grid's range that is examined at each end (0.02).

threshold

The posterior probability above which an end is flagged (0.05).

sd_g

The posterior mean and the 5% and 95% quantiles of the standard deviation of \(g\).

sd_g_prior

The 5%, 50% and 95% quantiles of the prior distribution of that standard deviation on this grid.

occupied

The proportion of the grid's range that contains the central 99.9% of the estimate of \(g\).

tau_c_over_sd_g

The standard deviation of a normal component divided by the standard deviation of \(g\) (NA for point masses).

The data frame grid$ends has the following columns.

end

"lower" or "upper".

value

The grid point at that end.

set_by

How the end was set: "support", "estimates", "pilot" or "true effects".

mass

The largest posterior probability that any site has in the outer 2% of the range at that end.

site, label

The position in the data and the label of that site.

estimate_beyond

How far the estimate of that site lies beyond the end, in units of its standard error (negative if it lies inside the grid).

sites_over

The number of sites for which this probability exceeds 0.05.

limits_at_end

The number of sites whose 90% interval has a limit at the grid point at that end when reading = "step" is used, because that grid point alone has at least the tail probability of the interval.

status

"ok", "warning" or "note".

Details

A diagnostic fails its check and is named in sampler_diagnostics_failed in two cases.

  • An R-hat value exceeds 1.05.

  • There is a divergent transition.

A diagnostic leads to a warning and is named in sampler_diagnostics_warned in the following cases.

  • An R-hat value is between 1.01 and 1.05.

  • A bulk or tail effective sample size is below 400.

  • An iteration reached the maximum tree depth.

  • The energy Bayesian fraction of missing information (E-BFMI) of a chain is below 0.3.

R-hat below 1.01 and effective sample sizes above 400 are the recommendations of Vehtari et al. (2021), and 0.3 is the value below which CmdStan warns about E-BFMI. The other thresholds are choices of this package. See vignette("diagnostics") for what to do about each kind of warning.

The sampler diagnostics describe the whole run, even if the fit was thinned. If the run has fewer than 400 draws in total, R-hat and the effective sample sizes are too unreliable to act on. Their values are still returned, but they are not compared with the thresholds, and diagnostic_skipped contains "rhat_check", "ess_bulk_check" and "ess_tail_check". Divergent transitions, the maximum tree depth and E-BFMI are checked regardless of the length of the run.

R-hat and the effective sample sizes are NA for a quantity that has the same value in every draw, e.g., the posterior mode of a site that never leaves one grid point in a fit with site_draws = TRUE. If a quantity is constant within each chain but differs between chains, the chains have not mixed and its R-hat is infinite. That R-hat is stored as NA, and "rhat" is named in sampler_diagnostics_failed even for a run of fewer than 400 draws. If R-hat or an effective sample size cannot be computed at all, or an effective sample size is infinite, all values of that diagnostic are NA and it is named in diagnostic_skipped.

The grid component contains the grid diagnostics. The main one is a check of the ends of the grid, i.e., its lower and upper limits. With point masses, the model places no effect beyond them. For each end, grid$ends gives the largest posterior probability that any site has in the outer 2% of the grid's range (mass). If this probability exceeds 0.05, the result for that site depends on where the grid ends, and the status of the end depends on how the end was set (set_by). Otherwise the status is "ok".

  • The status is "warning" if the end was specified in support or follows from the estimates alone (set_by is "support" or "estimates"). bayes_efron_fit() then issues a warning of class bef_warn_grid_ends that names the site, and "grid_ends" is added to sampler_diagnostics_warned, although it concerns the grid and not the sampler. A wider range may change the result, and compare_efron_grids() shows whether it does.

  • The status is "note" if the "pilot" method moved the end in (set_by is "pilot"). The pilot fit, which used a wider range, placed at most 0.05% of \(g\) beyond that end. A site with a large probability there has an estimate beyond the end of \(g\) and is shrunk to it, so the probability is reported without a warning. The same applies to a range around the true effects of a simulation (set_by is "true effects").

See the examples of plot.bef_grid_comparison() for a comparison in which the narrowest range gives a probability above 0.05.

No single number shows whether a range is wider than necessary. If there are few sites, the data carry little information about the parts of the range that contain no estimates, and \(g\) is determined by the prior there. The grid component therefore gives the posterior mean and 90% interval of the standard deviation of \(g\) (sd_g) next to the 5%, 50% and 95% quantiles of its prior distribution on the same grid (sd_g_prior). If the two are close, the data have hardly determined the tails of \(g\), and it is worth comparing fits with other ranges. The proportion of the grid's range that contains the central 99.9% of the estimate of \(g\) (occupied) is informative only if there are many sites.

Functions

  • print(bef_diagnostic): Prints the worst value of each diagnostic.

  • summary(bef_diagnostic): Returns a list in which rhat, ess_bulk and ess_tail are reduced to their worst value (the largest R-hat and the smallest effective sample sizes), with the name of the variable that has it.

  • as.data.frame(bef_diagnostic): Returns a data frame with one row per diagnostic and the columns diagnostic, value (the worst value), threshold, rule (whether value should be "at most" or "at least" the threshold) and status ("ok", "warning", "failed" or "not checked"). The last row, grid_ends, is for the end of the grid at which a site has the largest posterior probability in the outer 2% of the range. Its status is "note" if that probability exceeds the threshold at an end set by the "pilot" method or from the true effects.

  • format(bef_diagnostic): Returns the lines that print() shows as a character vector.

  • nuts_params(bef_fit): Methods for bayesplot generics, so that the bayesplot plots of sampler diagnostics can be made from a fit. nuts_params() returns the divergence indicator, the tree depth, the energy, the acceptance statistic, the step size and the number of leapfrog steps for every stored iteration, and log_posterior() returns the log density for every stored iteration. rhat() and neff_ratio() return, for each variable, R-hat and the bulk effective sample size divided by the number of iterations of the whole run. In a thinned fit (see thin in bayes_efron_fit()) the stored iterations are not consecutive, so a plot that compares each iteration with the previous one, such as bayesplot::mcmc_nuts_energy(), should not be made from it. nuts_params() throws an error if the fit does not contain the sampler quantities.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. and Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2). doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

See also

bayes_efron_fit(), plot.bef_fit_re(), vignette("diagnostics")

Examples

diag <- diagnose(krw_fit)
diag
#> <bef_diagnostic>
#> Model family: RE
#> Rhat max: 1.002 (log_g[97])
#> ESS bulk min: 1731 (lp__)
#> ESS tail min: 1780 (log_g[2])
#> Divergences: 0
#> Max treedepth hits: 0
#> E-BFMI min: 0.5682
#> Runtime: 0.7197 sec
#> Grid:
#>   lower end -0.0829: at most 0% of a site's posterior in the outer 2% (site "Safeway")
#>   upper end 0.1585: at most 0.1% of a site's posterior in the outer 2% (site "Genuine Parts (Napa Auto)")
#>   sd of g: posterior 0.01716 (0.01183 to 0.02396); prior 0.06991 (0.05814 to 0.07644)
#>   the central 99.9% of g spans 98% of the grid
#> Effective params: mean 46.67; sd 6.378

# The largest R-hat and the variable that has it.
summary(diag)$rhat
#> $value
#> [1] 1.001951
#> 
#> $index
#> [1] 105
#> 
#> $variable
#> [1] "log_g[97]"
#> 

# The three variables with the smallest bulk effective sample size.
head(sort(diag$ess_bulk), 3)
#>     lp__   lambda log_g[6] 
#> 1731.204 2082.036 2384.530
